verdict.reasoning: Patient reports cough and runny nose: 'I've just been having this like, cough, for quite a few days. And my nose is running.' Duration: 'a bit less than a week ago. Like maybe, maybe five or six days ago.' Cough characteristics: 'It's quite dry.'
Patient states: 'it's just all day, it like keeps me up at night as well, which is really annoying,' indicating nocturnal cough disturbing sleep.

Patient: 'the coughing is giving me a sore throat... just my throat is irritated from coughing. But it's not like, it's not that bad when I swallow or anything,' indicating irritation from cough without painful swallowing (no odynophagia).
Patient: 'I've been having like, like shivers... still you know, shivering a little bit.' and 'I haven't taken my temperature... But it feels like I probably did [have a fever].'

Fatigue: Doctor summarises 'quite lethargic and weak, you mentioned,' and patient: 'all I feel like doing is just lying in bed.' Myalgias: 'my muscle was really hurting... Especially like in my arms, my legs, like just everywhere basically.'

Dyspnea: 'Day to day when you walk around, uh you don't feel breathless do you?' Patient: 'I don't feel restless. No.' Chest pain: 'Any pain in your chest?' Patient: 'No not, not that either.' Ear symptoms: 'How are your ears?... No pain, no discharge coming from your ears.' Nausea/vomiting: 'have you had any nausea? Have you had any vomiting?' Patient: 'No. No, no nausea. No vomiting.'

'I had a little bit of diarrhea... Has that got better now, the diarrhea? Patient: 'Yeah, yeah. It got better. It was only like the first, like it started at the same time as the cough started. And then it stopped.'
Urinary symptoms: 'any problems with your waterworks at all?... your urine.' Patient: 'Ohh. Uh, no. No no, it's fine.' and confirms normal urination.
Patient: 'I have type two diabetes.'
Patient: 'And I have quite high blood pressure.'
Patient: 'I take Metformin for the diabetes.'
Patient: 'And I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure.'
Doctor: 'Any allergies at all, to medications?' Patient: 'No. No allergies.'
Patient: 'my dad also has type two diabetes.'
Living situation: 'just, it's just me and my partner.' Occupation: 'I am a developer.' and 'yeah. Work in IT.'
Smoking: Doctor: 'Do you smoke at all, April?' Patient: 'I used to, but I've stopped for about six months now.'
Alcohol: 'I don't drink more than like, like, let's say three evenings a week?... Wine, mostly.' and 'maybe two or three glasses' on those nights.
Doctor: 'I think based on your story, I think essentially I think you're, you're going through a bit of a bit of a viral illness.' This corresponds to a viral URTI/influenza-like illness assessment.

Control of diabetes: Patient: 'I have it under control. And since I've started taking this medication, I've just been like regularly checking that it, it's under control.' This supports T2DM stable on Metformin.
Hypertension: Patient: 'Same with the high blood pressure. Like I, I have it under control.' and is taking Lisinopril, supporting stability on this medication.

Doctor links alcohol to comorbidities: 'you're probably just about under the limit of... the recommended limit... something think about, just in terms of your blood pressure and diabetes, maybe something that you can maybe cut down on if you can,' indicating current use is above ideal for her conditions.

Doctor: 'things you can do to help yourself... get some nice, good rest. Drink plenty of fluids. Keep yourself well-hydrated. You can take regular Paracetamol.' Work: 'maybe take a day or two off work, if you can... and maybe think about work early next week.'

Doctor advises: 'If you feel like you're still not getting any better in two to three days, it's probably worth coming back to see me again... if you are still feeling feverish, um and your cough isn't getting any better, then we may look to give you some antibiotics for your chest.' There is no mention of ordering a chest X-ray (CXR), so including CXR is an added element.
Transcript confirms ongoing Metformin use and regular checkups, but the doctor does not explicitly state 'continue Metformin' or specify a plan for 'routine follow-up with PCP' during this encounter.
Although patient takes Lisinopril and reports BP is under control, the doctor does not explicitly instruct to 'continue Lisinopril' or 'monitor blood pressure at home' as part of this plan.

Smoking: prior cessation is noted but no explicit counseling to reinforce cessation is stated, so that part is not mentioned. Alcohol: Doctor advises, 'maybe for the first few weeks, why don't you cut down to two glasses a week. And then, one week thereafter... then you can maybe try and cut down altogether,' matching tapering wine to 2 glasses per week aiming for abstinence. Thus alcohol advice is supported; smoking reinforcement is an unstated addition but linked to existing cessation, so overall mostly supported with minor addition.
